column1: # The sweep behind LOOSE_MATCH_DISTANCE in brucellaid/mash.py. One row per public ENA read set,
# re-measured under the 2.1.0 k-mer copy threshold (one copy per 5x, 2 to 48).
# The threshold is the 95th percentile of the MASH distance of calls that AGREE with the ENA submitter:
# past it, the closest reference is further than a correctly identified library normally sits. Measuring
# that percentile over all 4,020 identified runs is not practical, so the population was binned by the
# distance each run had under the OLD threshold, a sample drawn from each bin, and each row carries the
# weight pop/n of its bin. Percentiles are computed on the weighted sample.
# submitted      the ENA submitter label, normalised to a binomial
# called         what BrucellaID called it, under the 2.1.0 threshold
# agrees         whether the two match, by the sweep's own rule
# distance_old   the distance this run had under the pre-2.1 threshold, for reference
# distance       the distance under the 2.1.0 threshold
# shared         min-hashes shared with the closest reference, of 1000
# weight         how many runs of the population this row stands for
# scripts/recalibrate_loose_distance.py computes the percentiles from this file.
